topics.topic: Definition, contents, and function-code accessibility of sandbox own_proc
questions: What is `own_proc`, what paths and information does it expose, and may function code read it or must every attempted access be a `sandbox_violation`?
What exactly is `own_proc`, and may function code or standard-library code read it despite the outside-path trap?
What concrete resource does `own_proc` require—such as a procfs mounted for the new PID namespace—and what paths and information may function code observe through it?

judgement.why: P8 decided the same own-proc mount, location, contents and accessibility question on the unchanged texts.

precedent.topic: Whether the sandbox must provide a private /proc or omit /proc
quotes: execute_function: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST start bubblewrap with new user, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces and no network interface but the new namespace's own loopback, which bubblewrap brings up, with no capability option, the environment cleared and then set exactly to the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant, exactly the host paths of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant bound read-only, inside the new root the symbolic links of the imported SANDBOX_ROOT_SYMLINKS constant (each name linking to its target, made by bubblewrap --symlink), one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write, bubblewrap's own fresh proc mounted at the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant and minimal dev mounts, and no other host directory; the child dies with its parent, and the runner is the init of the new PID namespace (bubblewrap --as-pid-1), so bubblewrap exits only after the host kernel has killed and reaped every other process of that namespace.

The place is now `SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT` in the data provider
    (`/proc`): `execute_function` mounts the proc there, `runner_arguments`
    passes it as the member `proc_directory`, and the runner lists it.
precedent.why: The later texts require bubblewrap's fresh private proc filesystem to be mounted at `/proc`.

topics.topic: Whether successful functions must remain deterministic for equal declared inputs
questions: Must equal function inputs still produce equal outputs, or may an untrapped source of time or chance produce different successful outputs that admission and runs judge independently?
Is equal-output determinism still guaranteed for every successful function execution, or may an untrapped source of time or chance produce different successful outputs and admission observations?
Is equal-output repeatability still an invariant for all implementations, or only for implementations that do not use an untrapped source of time or chance?
Does “pure” still include determinism with respect to declared inputs, or does it now mean only that effects, network, secrets and service handles are excluded?

quotes: The standard library's own entry points for the clock and for randomness raise in a function, so it cannot depend on the time or on chance by accident; code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.
6. The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
judgement.why: The changed product rule permits successful changing outputs obtained through an untrapped route, while A03's required test requires equal inputs to yield the same digest.

topics.topic: Classification of invalid calls to trapped clock entry points
questions: When one of the newly trapped entry points is called with missing, extra or otherwise invalid arguments, is the result a recorded trap and `sandbox_violation`, or an ordinary exception and `crashed`?

quotes: runner_source: [BEHAVIOR] The program MUST, before it loads the code, replace every entry point named in raise_on_call with one that raises whatever arguments it is called with, those in raise_without_argument with ones that raise when called without an argument, every method of the class named by raise_on_every_method, and the class named by raise_unseeded when constructed without a seed or with None, and that class's seed method when called on an instance without a seed or with None (A03 rule 4: an explicitly seeded instance draws no entropy and stays usable); and install an audit hook that raises on socket, subprocess and ctypes use and on opening any path outside the exchange directory and the readable_paths. Each trap first writes its hit to the channel, which the code cannot unsend.
judgement.why: The later runner note requires every raise-on-call replacement to trap regardless of the supplied arguments and to report the hit before raising.
